Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Rent Control Department summons hostel operators over illegal fee hikes Source : Ernest K. Arhinful 22 November 2026 5:39pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Rent Control Department has summoned managers of some university-affiliated and private hostels over unauthorised rent increases, with some operators reportedly raising fees by as much as 110 per cent.
The move follows complaints from tertiary students about sharp increases in accommodation charges and poor living conditions, Deputy Minister for Works and Housing, Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, has disclosed.
In a Facebook post on Saturday, November 21, 2026, she said the concerns were discussed during a working visit to the Department’s headquarters in Accra, where she met the Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, and other management officials.
During the meeting, Mr Opoku presented inspection findings showing that some hostel operators had increased charges by up to 110 per cent without the requisite statutory assessment.
The inspections also uncovered poor living conditions in some facilities, including inadequate ventilation, broken amenities and poor sanitation.
Mr Opoku further briefed the Deputy Minister on enforcement measures taken by the Department, including the issuance of summons to managers of facilities found to be flouting the regulations.
Ms Tetteh-Agbotui said the Department had also sought guidance from the Ministries of Education and Works, Housing and Water Resources to help address the situation.
She condemned the reported exploitation of students and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to strengthening the Department’s regulatory and enforcement efforts.
On behalf of the sector Minister, Ahmed Ibrahim, she assured students, parents, tenants and the general public that the concerns would be addressed through immediate, short-, medium- and long-term interventions.
The development comes amid growing concerns over the rising cost of student accommodation and the condition of hostel facilities in communities surrounding universities and other tertiary institutions.
